proposal: The Mandate recommends that NIH fund studies of the short-term and long-term negative effects of cross-sex interventions (affirmation, puberty blockers, hormones and surgeries) and of the likelihood of desistance when young people receive counseling without medical or social interventions (p. 462). It also recommends that the OASH Office of Science and Medicine lead an investigative literature review on topics including the effect of abortion on prematurity and breast cancer, evidence for gender-affirming care, and harms after cross-sex treatment in children, and that OASH withdraw its recommendations of and support for such interventions (pp. 490-491).

status_summary: Executive Order 14187, signed 2025-01-28, directed HHS to publish a review of the literature on best practices for children with gender dysphoria. HHS released the review on 2025-05-01 and a peer-reviewed version, now posted on the site of the Office of Population Affairs within OASH and dated November 2025; it finds the evidence for pediatric medical interventions to be of very low quality. NPR reported in April 2025 on a memo from the acting NIH Director asking for funding announcements on regret and detransition within six months, but no NIH funding notice or award was found, and no OASH review of abortion and prematurity or breast cancer was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14187 directed HHS to publish a review of the literature on best practices for children with gender dysphoria within 90 days (published in the Federal Register 2025-02-03).
HHS released its review, Treatment for Pediatric Gender Dysphoria: Review of Evidence and Best Practices.
timeline.source: HHS Office of Population Affairs (executive summary, which dates the original documents 2025-05-01)

timeline.event: HHS posted a corrected version of the review, with a peer review supplement, on the Office of Population Affairs site.

title: NIH studies of cross-sex intervention harms; OASH literature review and withdrawal
uncertainties: The order, the OPA page and the executive summary were read; the full report was not, and the executive summary says it contains no policy recommendations and does not address NIH or OASH. The 2025-05-01 date is given by KFF and by the executive summary, which refers to the May 1 documents, notes minor corrections on 2025-05-15 and carries a 2025-11-19 cover date; the OPA page prints November 2025. The NPR report on the NIH memo gives no memo date, so it is not in the timeline; it rests on two unnamed NIH staff and neither agency commented. The review was published by the Office of Population Affairs, which sits within OASH, but the Office of Science and Medicine role and any abortion-related literature review were not found. Searches run: three web searches (NIH regret study; HHS review; NIH notice) and Federal Register API queries. The December 2025 proposed rules on hospital conditions and Medicaid funding are tracked in c14-08. In review, the OPA report page was fetched on 2026-10-15: it names the report, says it was published November 2025 and is peer-reviewed, and lists an errata and a peer review supplement without dates. One further web search for an NIH funding notice on regret or detransition returned only syndicated copies of the NPR report. Primary-source lift 2026-10-18: the Federal Register record of Executive Order 14187 was re-read (Section 3 sets the 90-day literature review; Section 4 concerns grants to institutions and does not name NIH), the OPA report page was re-read (publication November 2025; errata undated; no mention of NIH or the Office of Science and Medicine), a Federal Register API query for NIH documents since 2025-01-20 on gender dysphoria, detransition or sex-rejecting terms returned zero results, the NIH Guide landing page lists no relevant notice, and one further web search returned only syndicated copies of the April 2025 NPR report. The NIH Guide search interface could not be queried for specific notices, so absence of a notice there is not confirmed.
